tag17_format.layout: u32 type=17, u32 size, u32 descriptor_size, u32 descriptor_version, then (size-16)/descriptor_size EFI_MEMORY_DESCRIPTORs (u32 Type, u32 pad, u64 PhysicalStart, u64 VirtualStart, u64 NumberOfPages, u64 Attribute)
tag17_format.observed_properties: sorted, non-overlapping, page-aligned, no zero-length; allowed types (1,2,7) all carry WB (attr 0xf) and no RUNTIME

boot_services_transition: VOS's Multiboot2 header requests only module alignment (6) and framebuffer (5), never EFI boot services (header tag 7) or the amd64 EFI entry (9); GRUB therefore calls ExitBootServices with the final map and passes that map in tag 17, and no tag 18 (boot services not terminated) appears. After ExitBootServices, UEFI defines BootServicesCode/Data as free for the OS, which is exactly where firmware drivers' DMA buffers (xHCI rings, AHCI command list/FIS) live.
intersection: every tag-6 available byte in [1 MiB, 1 GiB) is covered by EFI types {1,2,3,4,7}; every BootServices descriptor lies inside tag-6 type 1; tag 6 merges BootServices memory into 'available' (root cause)
before_first_allocation: the first PMM allocation is devmap_init's page directory, after pmm_init; exclusions computed by Rust before pmm_init and entered into the existing reservation table are applied by pmm_init's protect pass (clear-only), so they are active before any allocation by construction. Calling the freestanding Rust archive before pmm_init needs no boot-architecture change (no heap, no PMM, boot stack only).
other_types_policy: allowed only: LoaderCode(1), LoaderData(2), Conventional(7) with EFI_MEMORY_WB and without EFI_MEMORY_RUNTIME/EFI_MEMORY_SP; excluded where they overlap tag-6 available RAM: BootServicesCode/Data, Reserved, RuntimeServices*, Unusable, ACPI*, MMIO*, PalCode, Persistent, Unaccepted(15) and any unknown/OEM/OS type; tag-6 available RAM not covered by an allowed descriptor is excluded
